The IASB has issued three documents for comment to address issues stemming from the IASB's 2011 amendments to IAS 27 Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements. The three documents are:
Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements — Amendments to IAS 27, in response to issues raised by the European Commission (the EC) as part of its consideration of IAS 27 in relation to the European Council’s endorsement of IFRS 10 Consolidated Financial Statements, IFRS 12 Disclosure of Interests in Other Entities and IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement.
The amendments clarify and clarify the IASB’s 2011 amendments. The amendments relate to: (1) the consolidation and presentation of entities that have more than one class of equity investor (within a separate statement of cash flows); (2) the recognition and measurement of investments in associates that are subsidiaries; (3) the recognition and measurement of investments in associates in the statement of financial position; (4) the disclosures required for investments in subsidiaries and investments in associates; and (5) presentation and disclosures regarding subsidiaries and associates that are either (a) joint ventures, (b) unincorporated joint arrangements or (c) joint operating arrangements.
Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements — Interim Financial Reporting of a Subsidiary That Is a Parent Entity During Part of the Year — Amendments to IAS 27, which clarifies the treatment of a subsidiary that is a parent entity during only part of the year. The amendments reflect the IASB’s current policy that entities preparing interim financial statements should consolidate a subsidiary during part of the year using the same policy they would have applied had they prepared consolidated financial statements for that period.
Interest in Other Entities — Amendments to IAS 27, in response to the EC’s concerns regarding the IASB’s 2011 amendments to IAS 27. In particular, the EC’s concerns relate to the timing of the recognition of gains and losses on sales of investments in subsidiaries, investments in associates, and interests in joint ventures and joint arrangements, and to how such gains and losses should be presented in the income statement.
All of the amendments are effective for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2014 and interim periods within those annual periods.
